title: Window That Displays Both Asymptotes of a Reciprocal Function
originalTopic: Viewing window design with vertical and horizontal asymptotes
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x) = 1/(x - 2), identify the vertical and horizontal asymptotes, then choose a viewing window that shows the blow-up near the vertical asymptote and the flattening toward the horizontal one on both sides.

steps.title: Locate the vertical asymptote
steps.explanation: The denominator vanishes at x = 2 while the numerator stays nonzero, so the graph splits into two branches running off the screen there.
steps.why: A window must place the asymptote strictly inside the x-range, otherwise one branch is invisible and the curve looks continuous.

steps.title: Locate the horizontal asymptote
steps.explanation: Away from x = 2 the curve decays toward the x-axis, so y = 0 is a horizontal asymptote approached from above on the right and from below on the left.
steps.why: The end behavior is only recognizable if the x-window is wide enough for the curve to visibly hug y = 0.

steps.title: Choose an offset window
steps.explanation: The asymmetric x-range [-6, 10] puts x = 2 off-center with about 8 units of room on each side, and the modest y-range [-4, 4] shows the branches escaping vertically without compressing the flat tails.
steps.why: Deliberately clipping the vertical extremes is what makes both the blow-up and the approach to y = 0 readable in one picture.
